profiles.speaker: TED
profiles.accent: weathered north-east English coastal, broad flat vowels
profiles.timbre: gravelly, low and dry, with a smoker's rasp and a habit of coughing
profiles.voice_description: A gravelly older male, coastal accent: a weathered, low-pitched voice with a dry rasp, like salt and gravel in the throat. Slow, deliberate and sardonic, with a flat deadpan delivery and long grumbling pauses. Occasional grunts, wheezes and coughs. Volume rises to a hoarse bark when he shouts, but the pitch stays deep and the voice never gets light or bright. Close-mic, indoor warmth.
profiles.preview_text: Hrmph. The new guy. Storm season, and they send me a money toff in shoes like that. In. Mind the gull, he's the landlord. Boiler's cold and the beacon's starving. Hasn't eaten since the Pleistocene. Engine room, Isaac. Shovel coal. Quickly. It's sulking. Cracked clean through. The burner's finished. Hrmph. We need a new one.
canon_basis: chr_ted voice_casting_notes: 'gravelly older male, coastal accent'
Voices: gruff, snarky, old-school; grunts and coughs; introduces the setting and each objective
profiles.contrast_note: Lowest, slowest and most gravelly of the three, with dry deadpan delivery and coughs. Arthur is higher, reedier and faster. Daniel is young, light and bright. Even shouted, Ted stays deep and hoarse, so he reads as the heavy voice in a storm.

profiles.speaker: ARTHUR
profiles.accent: soft West Country sea-lilt, lighter and more musical than Ted
profiles.timbre: wiry, reedy, slightly nasal and thin, mid-to-high pitch with a cracking edge when shouting
profiles.voice_description: A wiry, old, frantic male voice with a soft West Country sea-lilt. Thin, reedy and slightly nasal, in a mid-to-high register with a rough crack when he strains. Quick and clipped, wry and friendly with a wary edge. Under pressure he turns breathless and shouts hoarsely over an engine, with fast rhythm and rising pitch. Calm moments are dry, steady and a little weary.
profiles.preview_text: Easy now, we mean no harm. Just cold and wet. And Daniel's been apologising to a seagull since the rowboat. Gate, please? Ted, you old rock. Thought you'd be drowned by now. Or at least moss. Keep her off the rocks, Isaac. Watch the water, not the dark. The dark's just showing off. Left! Your left! The left one!
canon_basis: Voices: older sailor, wry and frantic under pressure, friendly but wary; guides the crossing
profiles.contrast_note: Higher, thinner and faster than Ted's low rasp, with a lilting accent and a cracking, urgent edge. He is clearly older and more nasal than Daniel, who is smooth and youthful. His shouted lines are rough and reedy, never deep like Ted's.

profiles.speaker: DANIEL
profiles.accent: light, modern southern English, no strong regional marker
profiles.timbre: bright, smooth and boyish, light in the chest, with a slightly breathy, wavering quality when nervous
profiles.voice_description: A young, enthusiastic male voice, early twenties, with a light southern English accent. Bright, smooth and boyish with a slightly breathy quality. Light-hearted chatter that wobbles into anxiety: trailing off mid-sentence, nervous laughs, forced cheer, and whispering when spooked. Fairly quick and bouncy, with no rasp or grit. Higher and softer than the older men.
profiles.preview_text: Down here suits me fine. Did the walls just... never mind. Warm is good. I'm going to name the boiler Gary. Did you hear that? Tell me you heard that. Pipes, right? Say pipes. Don't listen to it. Wind makes all sorts of voices. Hum something. I'm humming. Arthur says it's just weather. I'm sure Arthur's right. He's usually right. Mostly.
canon_basis: Voices: younger sailor, light-hearted and anxious; shelters in the basement and stays there
profiles.contrast_note: The only young, smooth, bright voice, with no rasp, so he stands apart from both Ted's deep gravel and Arthur's thin old reediness. His nervous laughs, trailing sentences and whispers carry his anxiety. He stays in the basement, so he never competes with Arthur's storm shouting.

lines.tts_text: [grumbling] Hrmph. The new guy. Storm season, and they send me a money toff in shoes like that. In. Mind the gull, he's the landlord. [coughs]
Boiler's cold and the beacon's starving. Hasn't eaten since the Pleistocene. Engine room, Isaac. Shovel coal. Quickly. It's sulking.
[shouts] That's the firebox. Feed it coal, mind your sleeves, and don't make eye contact. It holds grudges.
[shouts] Also, if you hear singing down there, that's the pipes. Don't sing back.
There she goes. Keep shovelling. The needle is a coward and only moves when watched.
One shovel's worth. The old girl ate it and didn't even say thank you. Rude.
[shouts] Gauge is waking up. Nobody tell it what year it is. It'll want its pension.
[exhales] Hear that dynamo whine? That's joy, that is. Or a mouse in the works. Either way, she lives, and I'm putting it in the log as a miracle.
[sighs] Rowboat at my dock. Two men in it, wetter than the sea itself, which I didn't think possible. Go and let them in at the island gate.
[grunts] See them? Soaked and stranded. One of them's waving a sock like a flag of surrender. Gate's down the path. Go on.
Easy now, we mean no harm. Just cold and wet. And Daniel's been apologising to a seagull since the rowboat. Gate, please?
Good hands on that gate. Daniel, move. No, the other way. Quick, now.
Ted, you old rock. Thought you'd be drowned by now. Or at least moss.
[coughs] Thought the same of you. Hrmph. Dry yourselves.
[coughs] The boy can warm up downstairs. Boiler's finally working now it's fed. Don't tell it I said that. It's sensitive.
[sighs] I'll wait here until Daniel has settled in. He gets homesick in new buildings. He once cried at a staircase.
[nervous laugh] Down here suits me fine. Did the walls just... never mind. Warm is good. I'm going to name the boiler Gary.
[exhales] Dynamo's running and still no light. Something's wrong up top. Lantern room, Isaac. With me. Let's see if we can't get this old girl glowing.
[shouts] Arc lamp's in the middle. Let's open her up. It's an examination, except only one of us knows what they're doing. No offence, new boy. Actually, take offence. [coughs]
Cracked clean through. The burner's finished. [coughs] Hrmph. We need a new one.
[gasps] A passenger ship? Now? It's not in the log! Without the beacon she'll find the rocks. [shouts] Go, Isaac! Take the boat, take the sailor, take a coat!
[coughs] No burner, no beacon. There's a spare at the Saltgate. Go with Arthur, Isaac. He knows the way. He's also the only one who knows where the boat keeps its feelings.
In you get. One hand on the wheel, eyes on the rocks. Not on me. I'm not a rock. Ask Ted.
[hushed] There! Ship's lights, out in the swell. She can't see the rocks. No beacon. She's about as lost as Daniel in a staircase.
[shouts] Keep her off the rocks, Isaac. Watch the water, not the dark. The dark's just showing off.
[breathless] Too close! Give the rocks some room, Isaac. Plenty of time to hug them later.
[shouts] Hold on! Swing wide of the rock. Gently now. It's had worse.
Careful, Isaac! Far too close. One of them winked at me!
[shouts] Isaac! We'll be on the rocks! Steer away, steer away, now, now, now!
[shouts] Hold on, Isaac! She's taking a beating! Swing wide and steady her, quick! She's not even ours!
[breathless] She won't take much more! Get clear and steer true! I'm too handsome to drown!
Hands off now, you've done the steering, I'll bring her in while you get ready to jump. Try not to land on a fish.
Hands off now. That was rough going, Isaac. I'll bring her in; you get ready to jump. We only brushed the sea once.
[exhales] Hands off! You nearly wrecked us out there, Isaac. I'll bring her in; be ready to jump. I counted seven apologies owed to the rocks.
[shouts] Hands off, for pity's sake! You hit everything out there! I'll bring her in, you just be ready to jump! The sea sent a strongly worded letter!
There's the Saltgate quay. Fetch the burner. I'll keep the engine turning. Touch nothing you can't pronounce.
[exhales] That's it? Good. Hold it close. Back across we go. Don't sneeze on it.
[shouts] Straight down the middle! It's a corridor!
[shouts] Left! Your left! The left one!
[shouts] Bring her right! Right, now! Not wrong, right!
[shouts] Steady, middle! Don't you touch them! They bite!
[shouts] Hard left! Rocks to starboard! It's a rock convention!
[muttering] Nothing there for us. Leave it be. The burner, the burner.
[whispers] Don't listen to it. Wind makes all sorts of voices. Hum something. [nervous laugh] I'm humming.
[breathless] Did you hear that? Tell me you heard that. Pipes, right? Say pipes.
Arthur says it's just weather. I'm sure Arthur's right. He's usually right. [nervous laugh] Mostly.
Standing there won't warm the boiler. I tried it for a whole winter. Boiler stayed cold. I got a cold.
[grumbling] Basement, Isaac. Engine room. The coal's the big black heap. It's not a sleeping dog. Don't pet it.
[sighs] Engine room. Shovel. Firebox. In that order. I've written it on my hand in case I forget too.
I'll tell you what's down there: coal, a boiler, and my last shred of hope. Go and fetch all three.
I'm not angry, Isaac. I'm a lighthouse keeper. We don't get angry. We just glare, slowly, in a circle.
[exhales] Go down the stairs. They're the ones that go down. Isaac, I believe in you, which is a first for me.
Those sailors won't dry themselves on my dock, Isaac. I checked. For an hour.
[grumbling] The gate, Isaac. Down the path from the dock. One of them's started negotiating with the gate. He's not winning.
Walk to the island gate and open it. Let them in. Before they start naming the rocks.
I can hear them from here, and so can the fish. Isaac, the gate. It's a door that lives outdoors.
Ted wants that burner, Isaac. Boat's waiting on you. It's started tapping its foot.
[shouts] Come on! The Saltgate, across the Gullwater. Get in the boat. It's sulking. Everything here sulks.
Board the boat, take the wheel, steer for the Saltgate quays. Go!
Burner won't walk to the boat, Isaac. I've asked it. Twice.
[shouts] Find the burner! Keep looking. Look sharp! Look blunt, if sharp isn't working!
Find the burner, pick it up, and bring it to the boat.
[shouts] That's the jetty! Go, go, go. Don't you wait for me! I'll tie her up. Badly. Go!
[shouts] Bring the burner up here, Isaac! Don't you dare drop it! I've had a day, and it's only half over!
Socket's open. Burner in, and be quick about it. Slowly, mind. She's old. Quick and slow, Isaac. It's called finesse.
[hushed] That's the burner home. Stand back, Isaac. Give her room to wake. She's not a morning person.
She sees us! Look at her go, clear of the rocks. [laughs] You did it, you money toff.
[shouts] No. No, turn! Turn, you fool, the rocks! [whispers] Oh, no.
[sighs] That ship...we didn't get the burner out in time...those poor souls on board...we've failed...FAILED!!

suggestions: Audition each preview_text in Voice Design and generate 3 candidates per speaker. Pick the set where Ted is the lowest and slowest, Arthur the thinnest and fastest, and Daniel the brightest.
Check Ted and Arthur at storm volume with engine and rain mixed in. If their shouts blur together, push Arthur's pitch higher and thinner rather than louder.
Ted's muffled 'through the floor' lines (TED_S1_04, S1_04b, S1_05, S1_05b, S1_08) are best handled with in-engine low-pass and reverb on one clean take, not a separate voice.
The nudge ladders (S1_I1-I6, S2_I1-I4, ARTHUR_S3_I1-I3 and O1-O3) rise in stability as they get more explicit: wry or dry first, flat and clear last.
The three coastfolk voices are separated by pitch, texture and pace. The accents are deliberately light so they do not imply backstory about where the men are from.

Keep the delivery of TED_F_03 raw and breaking: it carries a single opening [sighs] tag so the script text stays exact, and the grief breaking into anguish on 'FAILED!!' can come from the capitals and low stability. Consider one take at lower stability and one safer take, and let the Story / Fail-State agent choose.
open_creator_decisions: Which lines are voiced and which are subtitle-only is a cost decision for the creator; every line here is prepared for ElevenLabs regardless.
Why Arthur and Daniel were on the water is left open, so no voice note implies smugglers or any backstory.
Ted and Arthur's relationship is still TBD in the lore. The 'drowned by now' exchange is a proposal, and the voices are cast as warm underneath without defining the history.
Final accents (north-east coastal for Ted, soft West Country lilt for Arthur, light southern for Daniel) are a casting proposal for the creator to accept or change.
Whether the supernatural ambiguity (wall whispers, singing pipes) gets any special audio treatment is left to the creator; no voice here confirms a cause.
